vo.text: Every order is a promise.
A date you gave a customer.
So when a port shuts down, the question isn't which ships are stuck.
It's which promises just broke.
This is Promise Graph.
Agents with a memory, built on FalkorDB.
Singapore's terminals go dark for five days.
One stuck shipment holds up the next, and the next, five steps down the supply chain, until it reaches a customer's door.
That's a graph. So we built it as one.
Customers, orders, promises and shipments, linked by what feeds what, in FalkorDB.
One variable-length query follows the delay, hop by hop, and keeps every promise that now misses its date.
755 orders. $114,065 in late fees.
Each one traced back to a shipment stuck in Singapore, on the real map.
Ask in plain English. The AI only picks a template. FalkorDB answers, and shows its query.
Why is Aisha's order late?
Here's her chain on a calendar: where each day of delay came from, and where buffer soaked some up.
Turn on Step by step, and the graph shows its work.
Flip the engine to Postgres, and the same question comes back with the same rows.
Compare puts both queries side by side.
Then six agents take over, and they coordinate through the graph.
Sentinel ranks the port with betweenness.
The Impact Analyst follows the cascade, and splits it with connected components.
The Rerouter finds shortest paths around the closure.
Finance prices every rescue.
And the Verifier re-checks every number.
Each one reads the last decision from the graph, and writes its own.
Spending money needs a person,
and whoever asked can't approve it.
Approved? Comms writes to the customers, and records how it went.
Because these agents remember.
In July, air-freighting containers around Suez didn't pay off.
So this time, Finance rescues three shipments by sea, for $19,180.
$68,257 saved. 406 orders back on time.
Every company gets its own graph, and its own memory.
We raced FalkorDB against a tuned Postgres with pgRouting.
Same data. Identical answers, checked row by row.
On the deep question, FalkorDB stays near 30 ms. Postgres climbs to around 100.
On clusters, pgRouting wins. We say so.
And we wrote minimal repros for three engine bugs we found.
That's Track two: agent memory and coordination.
Episodic, procedural and shared memory. Handoffs through the graph. A human gate. One graph per company.
And Track one: multi-hop reasoning, with graph algorithms as the agents' tools.
Promise Graph.
Know which promises broke, why, and the cheapest way to keep them.
